paper_summary: 7055 Al-alloy matrix syntactic foams reinforced with 1-2 mm Al2O3 hollow particles (52 vol.%) were made by simple gravity infiltration casting at 740, 770, 800 and 830 C, then normalized, annealed, quenched or solution-aged (470 C/1 h base). Average foam density was 1.73 g/cm3 with 40.89 % porosity. Quasi-static compression (1e-3 /s) gave the best as-cast properties at 800 C infiltration (yield 78.23 MPa, compressive strength 79.52 MPa, plateau 26.6 MPa); solution-aging gave the highest strength (95.32/96.45 MPa) and normalizing the best plateau stress (78.63 MPa) and energy absorption (48.14 MJ/m3, 28.04 kJ/kg).

extraction_notes: Process route: the paper uses gravity infiltration casting, which is not in the ProcessRoute enum (no applied pressure/vacuum), so process_route='other' for the primary records; the Table 8 rows for gravity/counter-gravity infiltration also use 'other', squeeze casting is mapped to pressure_infiltration and microwave sintering to powder_metallurgy. strength_mpa holds the reported compressive (peak) strength; the separately reported 0.2 % yield strength is included verbatim in each record's Table 6 evidence quote (740/770/800/830 C: 61.46/74.74/78.23/77.47 MPa; normalizing/annealing/quenching/solution-aging: 83.28/63.19/68.53/95.32 MPa). No elastic modulus, tensile or flexural data are reported. Densification strain converted from % to fraction. The 39-46 % porosity in Table 5 is the total foam porosity contributed by the hollow particles, not unintended matrix voids, so matrix_porosity_fraction is left null and the value is recorded in microstructure_notes. Particle volume fraction 0.52 is stated once in Sec. 3.3 ('the hollow particle volume fraction was 52 %') and applied to all primary samples. Particle true density is left null: Table 2 gives only a manufacturer range (bulk density 0.5-1 g/cm3); particle diameter is left null because only a 1-2 mm screened range is given, no mean. Test temperature recorded as 25 C for 'ambient temperature'. The 20 Table 8 comparison rows are literature values from other papers, marked data_origin='secondary' with the cited reference in sample_label; only density and energy absorption are given there (specific energy absorption in kJ/kg has no schema field, so it is kept only in the evidence quote). Two Table 8 entries report ranges (density 1.06-1.11 g/cm3 for ref [23]; W 20-35 MJ/m3 for ref [49]); those fields are left null. The 'Present work' row of Table 8 duplicates the normalizing primary record and was not repeated. Values in Fig. 6 and Fig. 7 were not digitized; all extracted numbers come from Tables 5-8 and the text.
